gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the PC-tethered laser scanners only work properly on Windows with a dedicated NVIDIA graphics card. Einstar's EXStar Hub lists an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 as the Windows minimum for Einstar 2, Rockit and EZ GO. Creality lists 'i7 7th Gen + NVIDIA (6GB VRAM)' as the lowest PC for Raptor X/Pro. Revopoint's 60 FPS GPU laser-scan mode for MetroX runs only on Windows with NVIDIA RTX (minimum RTX 3050 8GB, 32 GB RAM). Many shoppers' integrated-graphics laptops or MacBook Airs therefore don't meet the stated requirements.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited. 3dprinting.com/3d-scanners/ explains black and shiny surfaces (the pattern 'scatters or absorbs'), mesh hole repair and markers. On computers it only says 'a real RTX-class workstation outperforms onboard hardware' for post-processing, with no GPU minimums or NVIDIA-only requirement. 3dprinting.com/scanners/best-small-format-3d-scanners/ 'gives no hardware specs such as GPU, RAM, or CPU' and gives Mac support only for the Ferret SE and EinScan SP V2. Neither names a per-model GPU or macOS minimum. The surface-reflectivity mechanism is already covered by the rivals, so it wouldn't stand out.
decides: The shopper's computer decides between scanners before accuracy does. With an NVIDIA RTX 2060 or better on Windows, the Einstar 2 / Rockit and Raptor X/Pro are usable. A Mac user needs macOS Tahoe 26.2 or later and at least an M1 Pro/M3 with 16 GB for Einstar, and Einstar says 'MacBook Air is not among the recommended models'. Without a dedicated GPU, the Creality Otter and Ferret ('lowest' PC is an i5 8th Gen with 8 GB and no GPU listed, with Android and iOS support) or the standalone Einstar Vega are the safer picks. MetroX's fast laser mode needs an NVIDIA RTX card.
